title: A Third US Aircraft Carrier Arrives in the Middle East as Houthis Advance on Aden, China's October Economic Slowdown Deepens, and Hundreds of Thousands Rally in Prague
subhead: The aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt arrived in the Middle East as a third US carrier group while Iranian drones targeted a US base in Bahrain and Yemeni government troops pulled back from Bab al-Mandab to defend Aden; China's October industrial output and retail sales missed estimates while high energy costs pushed Japan's economy into a third-quarter contraction; and hundreds of thousands rallied in Prague to defend public media independence.

sections.heading: A Third US Aircraft Carrier Arrives in the Middle East as Houthis Advance on Aden and Iran Targets a Bahrain Base
sections.body:
Al Jazeera, Times of Israel, and Bloomberg — The United States Navy aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt arrived in the Middle East over the weekend to join two American carrier strike groups already operating in the theater, shoring up US Central Command firepower as Tehran warned it would not simply wait to be attacked. Bloomberg reported on Monday that Iranian forces targeted a US military facility in Bahrain with explosive drones—triggering civil defense alarms across the island kingdom—while simultaneously signaling to Washington that the diplomatic path toward a broader ceasefire arrangement remains open. Along Iran's western frontier, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps announced that its ground forces neutralized an armed PJAK cell affiliated with the PKK that had attempted to infiltrate the country (Anadolu Agency).

At the southern entrance to the Red Sea, Yemeni government forces withdrew from forward positions near the Bab al-Mandab Strait and regrouped around Taiz to reinforce the defenses of the interim capital Aden against a major Houthi ground offensive (Al Jazeera, Anadolu Agency). Houthi units subsequently fired ballistic missiles at the al-Qawa military camp in Aden and claimed coordinated missile and drone strikes against King Khalid International Airport and two oil pumping stations in Riyadh.
sections.whyItMatters: Deploying a third US aircraft carrier while Houthi forces push toward Aden and Iranian drones strike Bahrain shows that military pressure across both the Persian Gulf and the Red Sea is intensifying even as backchannel diplomacy continues.

sections.heading: China's Economic Slowdown Deepens in October and Japan's GDP Contracts as Beijing Confirms the Shenzhen Trilateral
sections.body:
CNBC, South China Morning Post, and Financial Times — Official economic data released Monday showed China's slowdown deepened in October as industrial production, retail sales, and fixed-asset investment all fell short of analyst forecasts, weighed down by a fifth consecutive year of property-market contraction that continues to erode household wealth (CNBC). Across the East China Sea, Japan's economy unexpectedly contracted in the third quarter after Tokyo allowed household electricity and fuel subsidies to expire in September, exposing Japanese consumers and manufacturers to elevated oil and liquefied natural gas prices driven by the eight-month Iran conflict (CNBC).

Against this fragile economic backdrop, Beijing formally confirmed on Monday that Chinese President Xi Jinping will host US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin for their first-ever trilateral summit in Shenzhen on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders' meeting (South China Morning Post, CNA, Financial Times). Meanwhile, at the 11-member ASEAN summit in Manila attended by Chinese Premier Li Qiang, US President Donald Trump, and Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. urged self-restraint and respect for international law to resolve South China Sea disputes (South China Morning Post).
sections.whyItMatters: Simultaneous growth setbacks in Beijing and Tokyo raise the economic stakes for Thursday's APEC summit in Shenzhen, where Xi, Trump, and Putin will test whether trade and security concessions can be linked.

sections.heading: Hundreds of Thousands of Czechs Rally in Prague Over Public Media Funding as Eisenkot Warns Netanyahu Threatens Fair Elections
sections.body:
France 24, Times of Israel, and Anadolu Agency — Hundreds of thousands of demonstrators filled the streets of Prague on Sunday to protest the Czech government's legislation to abolish independent public broadcasting license fees and place Czech Television and Czech Radio under direct state budget financing. Opposition lawmakers, journalists, and civil society groups warned that replacing public fee revenues with annual parliamentary appropriations would subject national broadcasters to direct political control, while government officials accused both public and private outlets of political bias.

In Israel, prime minister-designate Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party tasked with forming a new coalition, declared that fair and legitimate elections can no longer take place as long as caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu remains in office (Anadolu Agency, Breaking Defense). Eisenkot's warning coincided with Israeli media revelations that authorities are examining whether Netanyahu's office misused the Shin Bet domestic intelligence agency and national police following the October 27 election to manufacture a 'stolen election' campaign targeting high turnout among Arab-led parties (Anadolu Agency).
sections.whyItMatters: Mass protests in Prague and coalition turmoil in Jerusalem underscore growing institutional battles over media independence and electoral oversight inside parliamentary democracies.

sections.heading: A ULA Vulcan Rocket Failure Destroys 40 Amazon Satellites as Megaspeed Denies Spy Links in the Nvidia Scandal
sections.body:
South China Morning Post, Ars Technica, and The Guardian — A Vulcan Centaur rocket operated by United Launch Alliance, the joint venture between Boeing and Lockheed Martin, failed shortly after liftoff from Cape Canaveral, Florida, on Sunday, destroying a payload of 40 satellites for Amazon's Leo broadband internet constellation. The explosion marked the first total mission failure in ULA's 20-year history and dealt a blow to commercial and Pentagon efforts to maintain heavy-lift launch competition with SpaceX just one day after SpaceX caught its returning orbital Starship spacecraft in Texas.

In the technology sector, Singapore-based AI hardware lessor Megaspeed International issued its first public statement addressing the counterintelligence crisis that forced Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang to resign on Friday, insisting it is a 'legitimate and lawful business' and stating that suspected Chinese intelligence operative Alice Huang left the firm in late 2025 (BBC, The Guardian). While Elon Musk and more than 158,000 signatories backed an open letter calling on Nvidia to reinstate Huang, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged Nvidia's board to carry out a 'dramatic shake-up' ahead of this week's crucial Nvidia earnings report and Anthropic initial public offering (The Guardian, CNBC, Bloomberg).
sections.whyItMatters: ULA's Vulcan rocket loss leaves Western satellite operators even more reliant on SpaceX, while Megaspeed's defense and Treasury's call for a boardroom overhaul keep Nvidia at the center of US-China tech tensions.

sections.heading: Pope Leo Demands Justice for Slain Amazon Defenders in Peru as Mexican Cartel Founder Félix Gallardo Dies in Prison
sections.body:
The Guardian, Al Jazeera, and New York Times — Concluding a historic tour of Peru on Sunday, Pope Leo XIV traveled from the high Andes into the Amazon rainforest and delivered a forceful address condemning illegal gold mining and deforestation while demanding justice for murdered Indigenous environmental defenders, declaring that 'the blood of these brothers cries out.' In Mexico, federal prison authorities confirmed that Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo—the former Guadalajara Cartel leader known as the 'Boss of Bosses' who pioneered modern Mexican narcotics syndicates and was convicted in the 1985 murder of US DEA agent Enrique 'Kiki' Camarena—died in prison at age 80 (New York Times).

Elsewhere, independent Australian Member of Parliament Helen Haines was discharged from the hospital four weeks after losing both legs when she was allegedly struck by a car outside her electorate office (The Guardian, BBC), Myanmar activist Bo Kyi received the Ramon Magsaysay Award and urged ASEAN leaders to restore Burmese democracy (South China Morning Post), and garment factories across Bangladesh shut down as thousands of textile workers went on strike demanding a minimum wage of 30,000 taka ($245) per month (BBC).
sections.whyItMatters: From Pope Leo's intervention on Amazon resource extraction to labor strikes in Bangladesh's garment sector, social and environmental pressures are testing governments across the Global South.

bottomLine: Monday's global developments set a tense stage for Thursday's first-ever trilateral summit among Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen: the arrival of a third US aircraft carrier in the Middle East alongside Houthi advances on Aden and Iranian drone strikes on Bahrain shows the regional war remains volatile, while October economic slowdowns in China and Japan, ULA's Vulcan rocket failure, and the widening fallout from the Nvidia-Megaspeed espionage scandal highlight the economic and technological pressures converging on all three powers.
